## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by gray to gray-brown forewings with fine streaks, wavy lines, and woodgrain-like mottling that helps it blend into bark and dead leaves. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, yards, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where hardwood host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on leaves of woody plants and help move tree and shrub foliage into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
